newsitem.title: USA: Arrow Air links new road feeder service to Miami.
newsitem.headline: Arrow Air links new road feeder service to Miami.

text.p: Arrow Air Inc. has started a road feeder service designed to link the Southern United States with its Miami hub, a company executive said Friday.
"This is the groundwork to build new markets. We are already seeing a lot of new business," said Jon Batchelor, senior vice president of the Miami-based all-cargo airline.
Daily truck service will be available to and from Atlanta, Houston, Dallas/Fort Worth, New Orleans, Tampa/St. Petersburg, Orlando and Arrow's Miami hub.
The specially designed tractor trailer rigs will sport Arrow's logo, and will be operated by AeroTruck, a St. Rose, Louisiana, trucking company.
The airline also has instituted premium express service from these cities that gives a higher level of cargo service.
"Arrow recently was awarded U.S. government authority to operate between Miami/Houston and Lima and Iquitos, Peru," Ed Lesko, vice president-domestic sales said in a statement.
The road feeder will help start the Houston flights "as quickly as market demand requires," Lesko said.
The planned twice weekly scheduled service to Peru will begin by Decembver two. Arrow has been flying charters to Peru for some time, Batchelor said.

Arrow, which flies to the Caribbean and Latin America, carried the sixth most international cargo through Miami International Airport in the first nine months of 1996, according to statistics compiled by the Dade County Aviation Department. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
